keyFacts: A formal application letter has a fixed anatomy: sender block, date, recipient block, subject line, salutation, body, closing and signature.
The subject line is the most-read part of any application letter: make it specific, e.g. "Application for two days' leave" rather than "Leave".
One idea per paragraph keeps a formal letter readable; long single paragraphs are the most common formatting mistake.
"Yours sincerely" is the standard sign-off when the recipient is addressed by role ("Dear Sir/Madam").
Dates in formal letters are written out (18 October 2026), which this tool does automatically in each language.
A letter should fit on one page: if your points need more, attach a separate sheet instead.

application-letter-writer.workedExample:
Type: leave application. Name "Amit Kumar", recipient role "The Principal", organization "City Public School", subject "Application for two days' leave", points: "I need leave on 20 and 21 October 2026 for a family function." and "I have completed my pending school work." Date 18 October 2026.

Copy it into your email or print it.
mistakes: Sending the letter without reading it first — the tool drafts placeholder wording, not your story. A wrong name, date, or detail tells the recipient you never bothered to check.
Using 'Dear Sir/Madam' when you actually know the person's name — it reads as lazy. If you have the name, use it.
Sending the exact same job application to every company — recruiters can spot a generic letter in seconds, and it goes straight to the reject pile.
Writing a vague subject line like 'Application' — the reader learns nothing from it. Say what the letter is for in the subject itself.
Leaving a typo in a name, date, or notice period — small mistakes are the first thing people notice, and they quietly sink the whole letter's credibility.
